We went to ask two Lagos newspaper vendors, and the story they tell is different. By the time Nigerians were reading the news on their phones, the papers had already been in trouble for more than twenty years. Our new film follows that decline through the people who sold the papers every morning. It ends on the question that matters most for anyone who works in media here: if nobody pays for the news, who pays for the reporting? It is 14 minutes long. diaspora-investors-and-african-founders-.headline: Diaspora Investors & African Founders - Deals That Fell Apart
diaspora-investors-and-african-founders-.author: Brian M.
diaspora-investors-and-african-founders-.core: Posted in last 7 days Diaspora Investors & African Founders - Deals That Fell Apart Africans abroad send billions home every year. Many want to build something. Founders back home welcome the capital. Some of those deals fall apart. Nobody writes about them, and those are the ones I want to hear about. 𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗶𝗻𝘃𝗲𝘀𝘁𝗼𝗿’𝘀 𝘀𝗶𝗱𝗲: Months of silence after the transfer. Money that arrived and quietly became something else. Shares held informally by a relative nobody mentioned. 𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗳𝗼𝘂𝗻𝗱𝗲𝗿 𝗼𝗻 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗴𝗿𝗼𝘂𝗻𝗱 A new shareholder giving orders in a business they had never run. Weekly updates demanded by someone who didn’t see why a licence took four months. Dollars wired in, costs paid in a currency that moved overnight. A valuation that felt like a verdict on years of work. 𝗔𝗻𝗱 𝗼𝗻 𝗯𝗼𝘁𝗵 𝘀𝗶𝗱𝗲𝘀: A founder who felt questioned. An investor who felt ignored. A legal system neither side trusted to enforce anything. That is how deals between the African diaspora and private businesses back home actually fall apart. I’m researching where they break, and what would have saved them. The real stories and generic ideas. I’m looking for: - Diaspora investors who have put money into a business back home - Founders who have raised from the diaspora - Anyone who walked away from a deal or - Those who witnessed a deal fall apart. Comment below and I’ll message you, or send me a note directly. It can be a 20-minute call or a few written lines. Nothing is shared or attributed without your confirmation. Brian Mandisodza, CFA Inbridge Partners

icfcredentialed-coaches-conversations-wi.headline: ICF-Credentialed Coaches - Conversations With Coaches Series 2027
icfcredentialed-coaches-conversations-wi.author: Luba Diasamidze PhD, ICF PCC
icfcredentialed-coaches-conversations-wi.core: Posted in last 7 days ICF-Credentialed Coaches - Conversations With Coaches Series 2027 Dear LinkedIn community, we need your help! ➡️ We're looking for interview guest recommendations for our 2027 YouTube interview series, "Conversations with Coaches". So I thought, who better to ask than this wonderful community of coaching professionals? I've been reflecting on the conversations we've had over the past two years, and I'm genuinely grateful to all the amazing coaches who have joined us and so generously shared their experiences, perspectives, and the fascinating work they do. We've explored so many different niches, approaches, and ways of working with clients, and I think that's one of the things I appreciate most about this series. It gives us an opportunity, as a professional community, to expand our understanding of what's possible in coaching, where the boundaries of our profession might be, how coaching can be integrated into different contexts, and just how diverse the work of professional coaches can be. I hope these conversations also inspire other coaches to explore new possibilities in their own practice. And there's still so much more to discover! Our guest speaker portrait: ✅ We're looking specifically for ICF-credentialed coaches whose work focuses primarily on coaching clients rather than coaching education. ✅ Extensive experience with / focus on a particular coaching approach or client audience / coaching theme ✅ Geography doesn't matter at all. We'd love to hear from coaches anywhere in the world! The greater diversity, the better. ✅ Interviews are conducted in English ✅ We ask our guests to be willing to share the published episode with their own audience. We value reciprocity. Here are some of the niches and approaches we'd love to explore further: Coaching niches: Health coaching, Outplacement coaching, Outdoor coaching, Vision coaching, Coaching for teenagers, coaching for startups, etc. Coaching approaches: Group coaching, Narrative coaching, Schema-based coaching, Ontological coaching, Strengths-based coaching, etc. These are simply the areas that come to mind first, and we're absolutely open to hearing about other interesting work you're doing! As long as it has not been covered in the previous interviews. If that sounds like you, give me a shout! Or tag a colleague whose work you find fascinating and who you think may be interested in getting featured. I'd love to discover more of the incredible work happening across our coaching community! Huge thanks for all the guests who joined me over the past couple of years! It was incredible to learn from you! Ever wondered why making friends seemed so effortless in school and college, but feels like a whole exercise in your 30s? Could the answer lie in something as simple as proximity? I'm working on a feature exploring 'Propinquity' ; how being around the same people, sharing spaces and having repeated, everyday interactions can shape our friendships and help us build social circles, particularly as adults. I'm looking to speak with sociologists and psychologists who can help unpack this phenomenon and offer insights into how our changing lifestyles and social environments affect the way we form connections.
